definitions.explanation: The external appearance or outline of something.
The way something looks or is presented.

examples.japanese: {丸|まる}い{形|かたち}をしている。
この{石|いし}は{星|ほし}の{形|かたち}をしていて、{子|こ}どもたちに{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: This stone is shaped like a star and is popular with children.

examples.japanese: {形|かたち}だけの{謝罪|しゃざい}だ。
examples.english: It's an apology in name only.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}がようやく{形|かたち}になってきた。
examples.english: The plan is finally taking shape.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}い{出|で}を{形|かたち}に{残|のこ}したくて、{旅行|りょこう}の{写真|しゃしん}をアルバムにまとめた。
examples.english: I wanted to preserve my memories in tangible form, so I put my travel photos together in an album.

notes:
{形|かたち} refers to the external shape, form, or appearance of something.

COMMON SHAPE VOCABULARY:
- {丸|まる}い{形|かたち}: round shape
- {三角|さんかく}の{形|かたち}: triangular shape
- {四角|しかく}い{形|かたち}: square shape
- {星|ほし}の{形|かたち}: star shape

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {形|かたち}をしている: to have the shape of
- {形|かたち}になる: to take shape
- {形|かたち}が{崩|くず}れる: to lose shape
- {形|かたち}だけ: just for show, in name only
- {形|かたち}に{残|のこ}す: to leave in tangible form

COMPOUNDS:
- {形式|けいしき}: form, format
- {人形|にんぎょう}: doll
- {形容詞|けいようし}: adjective

COMPARE:
- {形|かたち}: shape, form (general)
- {姿|すがた}: figure, appearance (of people)
